# freecs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/freecs/2.3.0/freecs/

## Expand description

A high-performance, archetype-based Entity Component System (ECS) for Rust.

freecs provides a table-based storage system where entities with identical component sets are stored together in contiguous memory (Structure of Arrays layout), optimizing for cache coherency and SIMD operations.

[§](https://docs.rs#key-features)Key Features

- **Zero-cost Abstractions**: Fully statically dispatched, no custom traits
- **Parallel Processing**: Multi-threaded iteration using Rayon (automatically enabled on non-WASM platforms)
- **Sparse Set Tags**: Lightweight markers that don’t fragment archetypes
- **Command Buffers**: Queue structural changes during iteration
- **Change Detection**: Track component modifications for incremental updates
- **Events**: Type-safe double-buffered event system
- **Multi-World**: Split components across multiple worlds for >64 component types

The `ecs!` macro generates the entire ECS at compile time using only plain data structures, functions, and zero unsafe code.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use freecs::{ecs, Entity};
// First, define components (must implement Default)
#[derive(Default, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Position { pub x: f32, pub y: f32 }
#[derive(Default, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Velocity { pub x: f32, pub y: f32 }
#[derive(Default, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Health { pub value: f32 }
// Then, create a world with the `ecs!` macro
ecs! {
  World {
    position: Position => POSITION,
    velocity: Velocity => VELOCITY,
    health: Health => HEALTH,
  }
  Tags {
    player => PLAYER,
    enemy => ENEMY,
  }
  Events {
    collision: CollisionEvent,
  }
  Resources {
    delta_time: f32
  }
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CollisionEvent {
    pub entity_a: Entity,
    pub entity_b: Entity,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#entity-and-component-access)Entity and Component Access

```
let mut world = World::default();
// Spawn entities with components by mask
let entity = world.spawn_entities(POSITION | VELOCITY, 1)[0];
// Lookup and modify a component using generated methods
if let Some(pos) = world.get_position_mut(entity) {
    pos.x += 1.0;
}
// Read components
if let Some(pos) = world.get_position(entity) {
    println!("Position: ({}, {})", pos.x, pos.y);
}
// Set components (adds if not present)
world.set_position(entity, Position { x: 10.0, y: 20.0 });
world.set_velocity(entity, Velocity { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 });
// Add new components to an entity by mask
world.add_components(entity, HEALTH | VELOCITY);
// Or use the generated add methods
world.add_health(entity);
// Remove components from an entity by mask
world.remove_components(entity, VELOCITY | POSITION);
// Or use the generated remove methods
world.remove_velocity(entity);
// Check if entity has components
if world.entity_has_position(entity) {
    println!("Entity has position component");
}
// Query all entities
let entities = world.get_all_entities();
println!("All entities: {entities:?}");
// Query entities, iterating over all entities matching the component mask
let entities = world.query_entities(POSITION | VELOCITY);
// Query for the first entity matching the component mask, returning early when found
let player = world.query_first_entity(POSITION | VELOCITY);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tags)Tags

Tags are lightweight markers that don’t cause archetype fragmentation:

```
// Add tags to entities
world.add_player(entity);
// Check if entity has a tag
if world.has_player(entity) {
    println!("Entity is a player");
}
// Query entities by tag
for entity in world.query_player() {
    println!("Player: {:?}", entity);
}
// Remove tags
world.remove_player(entity);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#events)Events

Events provide type-safe communication between systems:

```
// Send events
world.send_collision(CollisionEvent {
    entity_a: entity,
    entity_b: entity,
});
// Process events in systems
for event in world.collect_collision() {
    println!("Collision: {:?} and {:?}", event.entity_a, event.entity_b);
}
// Clean up events and increment tick at end of frame
world.step();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#systems)Systems

Systems are functions that query entities and transform their components. For maximum performance, use the query builder API for direct table access:

```
fn physics_system(world: &mut World) {
    let dt = world.resources.delta_time;
    // Method 1: High-performance query builder (recommended)
    world.query_mut()
        .with(POSITION | VELOCITY)
        .iter(|entity, table, idx| {
            table.position[idx].x += table.velocity[idx].x * dt;
            table.position[idx].y += table.velocity[idx].y * dt;
        });
    // Method 2: Per-entity lookups (simpler but slower)
    let entities: Vec<_> = world.query_entities(POSITION | VELOCITY).collect();
    for entity in entities {
        if let Some(velocity) = world.get_velocity(entity).cloned() {
            if let Some(position) = world.get_position_mut(entity) {
                position.x += velocity.x * dt;
                position.y += velocity.y * dt;
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parallel-processing)Parallel Processing

Process large entity counts across multiple CPU cores using Rayon. Parallel iteration is automatically available on non-WASM platforms:

```
use freecs::rayon::prelude::*;
fn parallel_physics(world: &mut World) {
    let dt = world.resources.delta_time;
    world.par_for_each_mut(POSITION | VELOCITY, 0, |entity, table, idx| {
        table.position[idx].x += table.velocity[idx].x * dt;
        table.position[idx].y += table.velocity[idx].y * dt;
    });
}
```
Parallel iteration is best suited for processing 100K+ entities with non-trivial per-entity computation.

[§](https://docs.rs#command-buffers)Command Buffers

Queue structural changes during iteration to avoid borrow conflicts:

```
// Queue despawns during iteration
let entities_to_despawn: Vec<Entity> = world
    .query_entities(HEALTH)
    .filter(|&entity| {
        world.get_health(entity).map_or(false, |h| h.value <= 0.0)
    })
    .collect();
for entity in entities_to_despawn {
    world.queue_despawn_entity(entity);
}
// Apply all queued commands at once
world.apply_commands();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#change-detection)Change Detection

Track which components have been modified since the last frame:

```
// Process only entities with changed components
world.for_each_mut_changed(POSITION, 0, |entity, table, idx| {
    // Only processes entities where position changed since last step()
});
// Automatically increments tick counter
world.step();
```
Writes through `set_*`, `get_*_mut`, and `modify_*` mark the slot as
changed, as do spawns and component add/remove migrations. Raw table
access does not mark. Changed queries skip whole tables that no write
has touched since the last `step()`, using a per-table high-water tick
per component.

[§](https://docs.rs#system-scheduling)System Scheduling

Organize systems into a schedule:

```
let mut world = World::default();
let mut schedule = Schedule::new();
schedule
    .push("input", input_system)
    .push("physics", physics_system)
    .push_readonly("render", render_system);
// Game loop
loop {
    schedule.run(&mut world);
    world.step();
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#entity-builder)Entity Builder

```
let mut world = World::default();
let entities = EntityBuilder::new()
    .with_position(Position { x: 1.0, y: 2.0 })
    .with_velocity(Velocity { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 })
    .spawn(&mut world, 2);
// Access the spawned entities
let first_pos = world.get_position(entities[0]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(first_pos.x, 1.0);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#advanced-features)Advanced Features

[§](https://docs.rs#batch-spawning)Batch Spawning

```
// Spawn with initialization callback
let entities = world.spawn_batch(POSITION | VELOCITY, 1000, |table, idx| {
    table.position[idx] = Position { x: idx as f32, y: 0.0 };
    table.velocity[idx] = Velocity { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 };
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#per-component-iteration)Per-Component Iteration

```
// Iterate over single component
world.iter_position_mut(|_entity, position| {
    position.x += 1.0;
});
// Slice-based iteration (most efficient)
for slice in world.iter_position_slices_mut() {
    for position in slice {
        position.x *= 2.0;
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#low-level-iteration)Low-Level Iteration

```
// Include/exclude with masks
world.for_each_mut(POSITION | VELOCITY, PLAYER, |entity, table, idx| {
    // Process non-player entities
    table.position[idx].x += table.velocity[idx].x;
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#advanced-command-operations)Advanced Command Operations

```
// Queue batch operations
world.queue_spawn_entities(POSITION, 100);
world.queue_set_position(entity, Position { x: 10.0, y: 20.0 });
world.queue_add_player(entity);
// Check command buffer status
if world.command_count() > 100 {
    world.apply_commands();
}
// Clear without applying
world.clear_commands();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#event-management)Event Management

```
// Peek at events without consuming
if let Some(event) = world.peek_collision() {
    println!("Next collision: {:?}", event.entity_a);
}
// Check event count
if !world.is_empty_collision() {
    let count = world.len_collision();
    println!("Processing {} events", count);
}
// Drain events (takes ownership)
for event in world.drain_collision() {
    // Process event
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#conditional-compilation)Conditional Compilation

Both components and resources support `#[cfg(...)]` attributes for conditional compilation.
This is useful for debug-only components, optional features, or platform-specific functionality:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
ecs! {
    World {
        position: Position => POSITION,
        velocity: Velocity => VELOCITY,
        #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
        debug_info: DebugInfo => DEBUG_INFO,
        #[cfg(feature = "physics")]
        rigid_body: RigidBody => RIGID_BODY,
    }
    Resources {
        delta_time: f32,
        #[cfg(feature = "audio")]
        audio_engine: AudioEngine,
    }
}
```
When a component or resource has a `#[cfg(...)]` attribute, all related generated code
(struct fields, accessor methods, mask constants, etc.) is conditionally compiled.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.Entity.html)
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityAllocator.html)- Allocator
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityLocation.html)- Location
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityLocations.html)- Locations
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventQueue.html)- Queue
- Double-buffered event queue for inter-system communication.
- [Schedule](https://docs.rs/struct.Schedule.html)
- [Structural](https://docs.rs/struct.StructuralChange.html)- Change
- One structural mutation recorded by the world: a spawn, a despawn, or a
component add or remove. `mask`holds the components involved: the full mask for spawns and despawns, the delta for adds and removes. Consumers track their own`sequence`cursor via`structural_changes_since`and the owner trims consumed entries with`trim_structural_log`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [STRUCTURAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.STRUCTURAL_LOG_CAPACITY.html)- LOG_ - CAPACITY
- Backstop for worlds whose structural log is never consumed. When the log reaches this length it is cleared wholesale, so a world with no consumer stays bounded instead of leaking. Consumers that drain every frame never come near it.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [tick_](https://docs.rs/fn.tick_is_newer.html)- is_ - newer
- Returns true if `tick`was stamped after`since_tick`, treating ticks as a wrapping sequence so detection keeps working after`u32`overflow.

# car_proto - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/car-proto/0.32.0/car_proto/

## Expand description

JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol types for CAR client-server communication.

The protocol is bidirectional over WebSocket:

- Client → Server: session.init, tools.register, proposal.submit, verify
- Server → Client: tools.execute (callback for tool execution)
- Server → Client: execution.event (notifications)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [daemon](https://docs.rs/daemon/index.html)
- Mechanism helpers for the CAR daemon — URL parsing, probing,
and spawning the `car-server`binary. Hoisted out of`car-cli`and`car-ffi-common::proxy`(#139-fu1) so both sides share one implementation.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Create](https://docs.rs/struct.CreateHostApprovalRequest.html)- Host - Approval - Request
- Request to create an approval prompt in the host surface.
- [Execution](https://docs.rs/struct.ExecutionEvent.html)- Event
- Execution event notification (streaming).
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostAgent.html)- Agent
- Agent entry visible to menu bar, tray, or terminal host clients.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostAgentDisplay.html)- Agent - Display
- Host-visible display hints for an agent.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostApprovalRequest.html)- Approval - Request
- Approval request visible to the OS host surface.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostEvent.html)- Event
- Host event emitted to subscribed OS host clients.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostIdentity.html)- Identity
- Daemon-identifying metadata returned inside `HostSnapshot``car-server install`plus an ad-hoc eval daemon, etc.) tell which daemon they connected to and whether THIS one owns the supervisor lock or is observe-only. Closes the observability gap from Parslee-ai/car-releases#44.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostSnapshot.html)- Snapshot
- Snapshot returned by `host.subscribe`.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingConfigSetRequest.html)- Config - SetRequest
- Params for `messaging.config.set`. All fields optional — only the supplied fields mutate (a`null`/absent field leaves that part of the config unchanged).`add_handles`/`remove_handles`apply after`allowlisted_handles`when both are present.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingConfigView.html)- Config - View
- Result of `messaging.config.get`/`messaging.config.set`— the current (or post-mutation) view of the transport config. The active pairing code is intentionally NOT echoed here (it is surfaced only via`messaging.pairing.status`, mirroring the local-UI-rooted invariant).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingPairingStartResponse.html)- Pairing - Start - Response
- Result of `messaging.pairing.start`— the freshly minted, high-entropy pairing code to display ONLY in the local UI, plus the post-mint view.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingPairingStatusResponse.html)- Pairing - Status - Response
- Result of `messaging.pairing.status`— whether a pairing is in flight and, when so, the active code (host/local-auth gated read only, so the local UI can re-display the code after a reload).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingStatusView.html)- Status - View
- Result of `messaging.status`— the real runtime liveness of a channel’s approval transport, computed daemon-side (U2). The host UI renders a SINGLE readiness state from this object rather than re-deriving “is it on” from scattered permission widgets (the scatter that produced the confusing pane).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingTestSendResponse.html)- Test - Send - Response
- Result of `messaging.test_send`— the synchronous outcome of the on-demand self-test (U4).`ok:true`means the labeled test message was delivered to the paired handle;`ok:false`carries an actionable`error`(channel off, no paired handle, Automation denied, recipient-not-found). The self-test mints NO approval/pairing mapping and resolves nothing.
- [Parslee](https://docs.rs/struct.ParsleeIdentity.html)- Identity
- Parslee cloud identity associated with the local CAR user.
- [Policy](https://docs.rs/struct.PolicyDefinition.html)- Definition
- Policy definition from client.
- [Policy](https://docs.rs/struct.PolicyRejection.html)- Rejection
- A policy rejection captured on a turn (R2 / R11). When an action is
`ActionStatus::Rejected`, the tool body never ran, so`cli_outcome`is forced to`not-run`and the rejection is recorded here.
- [Proposal](https://docs.rs/struct.ProposalSubmitRequest.html)- Submit - Request
- Submit a proposal for execution.
- [Register](https://docs.rs/struct.RegisterHostAgentRequest.html)- Host - Agent - Request
- Request to register an agent with the OS host surface.
- [Resolve](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolveHostApprovalRequest.html)- Host - Approval - Request
- Request to resolve an approval.
- [RunComplete](https://docs.rs/struct.RunCompleteRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.complete`request params.
- [RunComplete](https://docs.rs/struct.RunCompleteResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.complete`response.
- [RunEnded](https://docs.rs/struct.RunEnded.html)
- A run reached a terminal state — recorded on `runs.complete`(with a reported outcome) or on a mid-run disconnect (as`Incomplete`).
- [RunGet](https://docs.rs/struct.RunGetTraceRequest.html)- Trace - Request
- `runs.get_trace`request params — fetch a run’s full ordered trace.
- [RunList](https://docs.rs/struct.RunListRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.list`request params — list an agent’s runs newest-first.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.RunRecordTurnsRequest.html)- Turns - Request
- `runs.record_turns`request params — a WS-only batch append of client-narrated turns to a run the calling connection owns. The agent builds full- `RunTurn`s itself (out-of-pipeline capture: its work happens inside its own subprocess, never through- `proposal.submit`), then pushes them here in batches. The daemon owns the turn- `index`(re-stamped under the- `runs`lock — the client’s- `index`values are ignored), the per-field/per-turn byte caps, the batch-size cap, and the per-run turn ceiling; it appends through the same- `record_run_turns`path the proposal recorder uses, so persistence and- `runs.trace.event`fanout are identical. Turn content beyond size is intentional pass-through — the daemon validates size and ownership, never semantics.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.RunRecordTurnsResponse.html)- Turns - Response
- `runs.record_turns`response.
- [RunStart](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStartRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.start`request params.
- [RunStart](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStartResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.start`response.
- [RunStarted](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStarted.html)
- A run began — recorded when `runs.start`mints the`run_id`.
- [RunSubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunSubscribeRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.subscribe`request params.
- [RunSubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunSubscribeResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.subscribe`response — the snapshot-at-cursor the client folds before the live- `runs.trace.event`stream starts.
- [RunTrace](https://docs.rs/struct.RunTraceEvent.html)- Event
- One `runs.trace.event`server → client notification (agent run tracing, U4). Pushed to every`(host_client, run_id)`subscriber.
- [RunTurn](https://docs.rs/struct.RunTurn.html)
- One captured turn of a run — one action of one submitted proposal.
- [RunUnsubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunUnsubscribeRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.unsubscribe`request params.
- [RunUnsubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunUnsubscribeResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.unsubscribe`response.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionInitRequest.html)- Init - Request
- Initialize a session.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionInitResponse.html)- Init - Response
- [SetHost](https://docs.rs/struct.SetHostAgentStatusRequest.html)- Agent - Status - Request
- Request to update an agent’s host-visible status.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolCancelRequest.html)- Cancel - Request
- Fire-and-forget `tools.cancel`notification (Parslee-ai/car#264).
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolDefinition.html)- Definition
- Tool definition sent by client during registration.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolExecuteRequest.html)- Execute - Request
- Server asks client to execute a tool.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolExecuteResponse.html)- Execute - Response
- Client returns tool execution result.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolRateLimit.html)- Rate - Limit
- Mirror of `car_ir::ToolRateLimit`over the wire.
- [Verify](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifyIssueProto.html)- Issue - Proto
- [Verify](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifyRequest.html)- Request
- Verify a proposal without executing.
- [Verify](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifyResponse.html)- Response

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [CliOutcome](https://docs.rs/enum.CliOutcome.html)
- How a CLI-driving action (e.g. Bulldozer’s `drive_cli`) terminated.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostAgentStatus.html)- Agent - Status
- OS-host-visible agent status.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostApprovalStatus.html)- Approval - Status
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostManifestRole.html)- Manifest - Role
- Manifest-lock relationship for the daemon serving this WS.
Returned inside `HostIdentity`
- [RunLive](https://docs.rs/enum.RunLiveStatus.html)- Status
- Coarse live status of a run for the subscribe snapshot and each
`runs.trace.event`. Distinct from the run-level`OutcomeStatus`carried inside a terminal`RunTermination::Outcome`— this is the “is the run still open?” signal the live client folds into its view. Mirrors`RunStore::RunStatus`but lives in`car-proto`so the wire shape doesn’t depend on the server-core crate.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/enum.RunRecord.html)
- One durable run record. U1 ships `Started`/`Ended`; U2 adds the per-turn`Turn`variant. Tagged on`record`so adding a variant is forward-compatible on the wire.
- [RunTermination](https://docs.rs/enum.RunTermination.html)
- How a run reached its terminal state.
- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/enum.VerifierVerdict.html)- Verdict
- The verifier verdict for a turn — Bulldozer’s `check_outcome`result.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [PROTOCOL_](https://docs.rs/constant.PROTOCOL_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- Wire protocol version for the daemon JSON-RPC protocol. Bump ONLY on a
backward-incompatible change to the request/response shapes or method
semantics (NOT on every release — this is independent of the package
semver). Client and server exchange this in the `server.handshake`RPC so version drift FAILS LOUD with a clear error instead of silently misbehaving or hanging.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [deterministic_](https://docs.rs/fn.deterministic_run_id.html)- run_ - id
- Compute a deterministic, content-derived run id (EPIC B / B7).

# vvm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vvm-rs/0.1.0-alpha.1/vvm/

## Expand description

Verilator Verification Methodology for Rust.

VVM provides strongly typed Rust testbenches for Verilator-generated HDL models.

Tests marked with `#[vvm::test]` become ordinary Rust `#[test]` functions.
Place unit-style VVM tests inside an explicit `#[cfg(test)]` module. Cargo
integration tests under `tests/` do not need an additional `cfg(test)`.
Standard Rust tooling such as `cargo test` and `cargo nextest run` owns test
discovery, filtering, and execution.

The runtime facade exposes:

- generated DUT integration;
- typed stimulus driving and output sampling;
- synchronous clock control;
- stateful reference models;
- scoreboards and structured mismatches;
- deterministic testbench execution.

Native compilation and DUT generation are configured separately through
the `vvm-build` crate from a consuming package’s `build.rs`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

A build script describes the DUT:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use vvm_build::{BuildResult, DutBuilder};
fn main() -> BuildResult<()> {
    DutBuilder::new("counter")
        .top_module("counter")
        .source("rtl/counter.sv")
        .build()
}
```
The generated DUT can then be included and verified:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[cfg(test)]
mod vvm_tests {
    use vvm::prelude::*;
    vvm::include_dut!(counter);
    use counter::Counter;
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Drive)]
    #[vvm(dut = Counter)]
    struct CounterStimulus {
        #[vvm(port)]
        reset_n: bool,
        #[vvm(port)]
        enable: bool,
    }
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Sample)]
    #[vvm(dut = Counter)]
    struct CounterObservation {
        #[vvm(port)]
        count: u8,
    }
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Clock)]
    #[vvm(
        dut = Counter,
        clock = "clk"
    )]
    struct CounterClock;
    /// Counter smoke verification.
    #[vvm::test(trace)]
    fn counter_smoke(config: &vvm::TestRunConfig) -> Result<CounterTestResult> {
        let mut dut = Counter::new()?;
        config.configure_trace(&mut dut)?;
        Ok(
            Testbench::new(dut)
                // ...
                .run::<CounterObservation>(),
        )
    }
}
```

# noxu_persist_derive - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-persist-derive/7.2.2/noxu_persist_derive/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

Derive macros for the Noxu DB Direct Persistence Layer (DPL).

This crate provides three `#[derive(...)]` macros that generate the
boilerplate required to use a Rust struct with `noxu-persist`:

-
`#[derive(Entity)]``noxu_persist::Entity`for a user struct. The struct must have exactly one field annotated with`#[primary_key]`; the field’s type becomes`Entity::PrimaryKey`. By default the entity name is the struct name; override with`#[entity(name = "...")]`at the struct level.
-
`#[derive(PrimaryKey)]``noxu_persist::PrimaryKey`for a user struct used as a*composite*or*newtype*primary key (analogue of`@KeyField`from BDB-JE). Supports tuple structs with one field (newtype) and named-field structs (composite, length-prefix concatenation). The struct must also derive`Clone + PartialEq + Eq + Hash`for the`PrimaryKey`trait bounds; this is the user’s responsibility.
-
`#[derive(SecondaryKey)]``#[secondary_key(...)]`field on the user struct, emits a typed`Foo::open_<name>_index(primary)`helper method that opens a`noxu_persist::SecondaryIndex`against a`PrimaryIndex`, plus a`pub const SECONDARY_INDEXES: &'static [SecondarySpec]`table describing every declared index. This derive is independent of`derive(Entity)`(you can use either or both).

[§](https://docs.rs#why-three-macros)Why three macros?

BDB-JE has three annotations: `@Entity`, `@PrimaryKey`,
`@SecondaryKey` — each addressing a different concern.  The Noxu
port preserves the same factoring so the porting guidance is
mechanical:

| JE annotation | Noxu derive |
|---|---|
| `@Entity` | `#[derive(Entity)]`(struct level) |
| `@PrimaryKey`(field) | `#[primary_key]`(consumed by`Entity`derive) |
| `@PrimaryKeyField`/`@KeyField` | `#[derive(PrimaryKey)]`(struct level for composite key types) |
| `@SecondaryKey(name=…, relate=…, …)` | `#[secondary_key(name=…, relate=…, …)]`(field level, consumed by`SecondaryKey`derive) |

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-path-escape-hatch)Crate-path escape hatch

By default the generated code emits `::noxu::persist::…` paths, so
the `noxu` umbrella crate must be in the dependency graph.  Users who
depend on `noxu-persist` **directly** (without the umbrella) can
override this with the `crate` key inside the `#[entity(…)]`
container attribute:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Cargo.toml: noxu-persist = "3"  (no noxu umbrella needed)
use noxu_persist::{Entity, PrimaryKey, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PrimaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct UserId(u64);
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: UserId,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
}
```
The `crate` key is accepted by all three derives via the
`#[entity(crate = "…")]` form.  A string literal containing a valid
Rust module path is required (validated at compile time); a malformed
path produces a descriptive compile error.

[§](https://docs.rs#re-exports)Re-exports

The `noxu-persist` crate re-exports all three derives so users only
need a single dependency:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_persist::{Entity, PrimaryKey, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: u64,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_dept", relate = ManyToOne, related_entity = "Department")]
    dept: Option<u64>,
}
```
## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Entity](https://docs.rs/derive.Entity.html)
- Derive `noxu_persist::Entity`for a struct.
- [Primary](https://docs.rs/derive.PrimaryKey.html)- Key
- Derive `noxu_persist::PrimaryKey`for a custom key struct.
- [Secondary](https://docs.rs/derive.SecondaryKey.html)- Key
- Derive secondary-index helpers for fields annotated with
`#[secondary_key(...)]`.

# weathervane - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/weathervane/0.9.1/weathervane/

## Expand description

Weather domain logic for the weathervane family of applications.

This crate is purely reactive: no polling, no timers, no config storage. It exposes async functions that frontends call when they decide it’s time. The frontend owns all scheduling, config persistence, and passes the relevant parameters (coordinates, units, etc.) on each call.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# car_integrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/car-integrations/0.32.0/car_integrations/

## Expand description

Account-bound integrations for Common Agent Runtime: Calendar, Contacts, Mail, Messages.

The logical capabilities are the same on every OS; the backends are
not. v1 defines the release contract — stable return shapes that carry
explicit `available` + `backend` fields so downstream apps can branch
cleanly while backends light up incrementally.

[§](https://docs.rs#backends-target)Backends (target)

| OS | Calendar | Contacts | Messages | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| macOS | EventKit (EKEventStore) | Contacts.framework | Mail.app automation | Messages.app automation |
| Windows | MS Graph + Outlook MAPI | Windows.Contacts + Graph | MS Graph + MAPI | Not modeled |
| Linux | Evolution DS + CalDAV | Evolution DS + CardDAV | Evolution DS + IMAP | Not modeled |

Backends return Unavailable-with-reason so callers can distinguish missing OS configuration, denied TCC access, and unmodeled platforms.

[§](https://docs.rs#dependencies-and-honest-gaps)Dependencies (and honest gaps)

Full operation needs:

- **car-secrets**— where credentials and tokens live
- **car-accounts**— to know which account the call should be bound to
- **car-permissions**— to preflight OS consent before the side effect

The macOS backends compose these where the OS exposes a useful native surface; other platforms are still modeled but not fully implemented.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [apple](https://docs.rs/apple/index.html)
- macOS account-backed Apple app integrations not covered by Calendar, Contacts, Mail, or Messages.
- [calendar](https://docs.rs/calendar/index.html)
- Calendar capability — list calendars, list upcoming events.
- [contacts](https://docs.rs/contacts/index.html)
- Contacts capability — enumerate containers, query contacts.
- [mail](https://docs.rs/mail/index.html)
- Mail capability — enumerate accounts, summarize inbox, send/draft.
- [messages](https://docs.rs/messages/index.html)
- Messages capability — enumerate Messages.app services/chats and send.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Availability](https://docs.rs/struct.Availability.html)
- Availability envelope — returned from every list-ish method so callers
can branch on `available`instead of assuming a populated list.

# noxu_collections - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-collections/7.2.2/noxu_collections/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

Iterator-based collection views for Noxu DB.

Provides typed map / set / list / iterator views over Noxu DB databases, allowing database records to be accessed through familiar Rust collection patterns.

Every `Stored*` type is parameterised by [ noxu_bind::EntryBinding](https://docs.rs/noxu-bind/7.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/noxu_bind/entry_binding/trait.EntryBinding.html)
implementations for keys and/or values; the public methods are
generic over the typed

`K` / `V` rather than over `&[u8]`.  Every
method accepts `txn: Option<&noxu_db::Transaction>` as the leading
argument — the same convention as `noxu_db::Database` /
`noxu_db::SecondaryDatabase`:- `None`runs the operation as auto-commit (the engine allocates a synthetic auto-txn for each call).
- `Some(&t)`participates in the caller’s transaction.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

- `StoredMap<K, V, KB, VB>`
- `StoredSortedMap<K, V, KB, VB>`- `first_key`,- `last_key`,- `iter_from`,- `iter_reverse`).
- `StoredKeySet<K, KB>`
- `StoredValueSet<V, VB>`
- `StoredList<V, VB>`- `remove`.
- `StoredIterator<T>`
- `TransactionRunner`- `&Transaction`it supplies can be threaded straight into any Stored* method.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_bind::{IntBinding, StringBinding};
use noxu_collections::{StoredMap, TransactionRunner};
use noxu_db::{DatabaseConfig, Environment, EnvironmentConfig};
let env = Environment::open(env_config)?;
let db_config = DatabaseConfig::new().with_allow_create(true).with_transactional(true);
let db  = env.open_database(None, "users", &db_config)?;
let map: StoredMap<i32, String, _, _> =
    StoredMap::new(&db, IntBinding, StringBinding);
// Auto-commit:
map.put(None, &1, &"alice".to_string())?;
// Participate in a runner-managed txn:
let runner = TransactionRunner::new(&env);
runner.run(|txn| {
    map.put(Some(txn), &2, &"bob".to_string())?;
    map.remove(Some(txn), &1)?;
    Ok(())
})?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#migration-from-v15)Migration from v1.5

The v1.5 → v1.6 transition breaks the v1.5 `&[u8]`-keyed surface.  See
`docs/src/getting-started/migrating.md` for the detailed
before/after.  In short:

- `StoredMap::new(&db, false)`→- `StoredMap::new(&db, key_binding, value_binding)`.
- `map.get(b"k")`→- `map.get(None, &k)`.
- The internal `BTreeSet`key index,`register_key`/`register_keys`/`known_keys`accessors are removed. Iteration walks the database directly via a cursor.
- `StoredList::remove`now shifts every higher index down by one slot and decrements- `next_index`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [CollectionError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.CollectionError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html);
- `pub use stored_iterator::`- [StoredIterator](https://docs.rs/stored_iterator/struct.StoredIterator.html);
- `pub use stored_key_set::`- [StoredKeySet](https://docs.rs/stored_key_set/struct.StoredKeySet.html);
- `pub use stored_list::`- [StoredList](https://docs.rs/stored_list/struct.StoredList.html);
- `pub use stored_map::`- [StoredMap](https://docs.rs/stored_map/struct.StoredMap.html);
- `pub use stored_sorted_map::`- [StoredSortedMap](https://docs.rs/stored_sorted_map/struct.StoredSortedMap.html);
- `pub use stored_value_set::`- [StoredValueSet](https://docs.rs/stored_value_set/struct.StoredValueSet.html);
- `pub use transaction_runner::`- [RetryConfig](https://docs.rs/transaction_runner/struct.RetryConfig.html);
- `pub use transaction_runner::`- [TransactionRunner](https://docs.rs/transaction_runner/struct.TransactionRunner.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types for the collections crate.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_iterator/index.html)- iterator
- Typed iterators for `noxu-collections`Stored* views.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_key_set/index.html)- key_ - set
- Typed key-set view of a database.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_list/index.html)- list
- Typed list view of a database.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_map/index.html)- map
- Typed map view of a database.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_sorted_map/index.html)- sorted_ - map
- Typed sorted-map view of a database.
- [stored_](https://docs.rs/stored_value_set/index.html)- value_ - set
- Typed value-collection view of a database.
- [transaction_](https://docs.rs/transaction_runner/index.html)- runner
- Transaction execution helper with deadlock-aware retry and exponential backoff.

# car-daemon-client 0.32.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/car-daemon-client/0.32.0

# car-daemon-client

The WebSocket JSON-RPC client core every CAR FFI binding proxies
through to reach the singleton `car-server` daemon. Extracted verbatim
from `car-ffi-common` (which re-exports both modules, so existing
`car_ffi_common::proxy::…` / `car_ffi_common::auth_token::…` import
paths keep working) so the UniFFI Swift / Kotlin surface can speak to
the daemon without absorbing car-ffi-common's transitive dependency
tree — car-voice (whisper-rs, coreaudio-sys), car-browser, car-vision
are wrong for `aarch64-apple-ios` and unnecessary for a pure WS
client. The only internal dependency is `car-proto`.

## Modules

- `proxy`- `DaemonClient`: one persistent WebSocket per consumer, id-routed request/response multiplexing, the- `session.auth`+- `server.handshake`connect sequence (automatic token resolution, supervised-agent attach via- `CAR_AGENT_ID`/- `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN`, or an explicit token via- `with_url_and_token`), server-initiated request handlers (- `tools.execute`reverse-calls from the daemon's- `WsToolExecutor`), notification handlers (- `voice.event`,- `a2ui.event`, …), per-method read-timeout derivation (- `proposal.submit`budgets,- `infer`cold-load floor +- `infer.progress`idle-reset heartbeats), and the- `proxy_*`per-method wrappers the bindings dispatch to.
- `auth_token`- `0600`file; DPAPI-encrypted at rest on Windows;- `$CAR_AUTH_TOKEN`override for cross-host clients).

## Consumers

- `car-ffi-common`(re-export; NAPI + PyO3 dispatch through it)
- `car-ffi-uniffi`(- `CarDaemonClient`— the Swift/Kotlin daemon-client mode)
- `car-server`,- `car-cli`,- `car-registry`(via the- `car-ffi-common`re-export paths)

## Contract notes

The daemon scopes sessions to the WebSocket connection: state,
registered tools, policies, and the per-session memgine die with the
socket. Keep one `DaemonClient` per logical consumer for the process
lifetime; it lazy-connects on first call and reconnects (fresh
session) after a transport failure. See `docs/websocket-protocol.md`
for the wire protocol.

#
                    car-daemon-client 0.32.0

# base64 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base64/^0.22/

## Expand description

Correct, fast, and configurable [base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64) decoding and encoding. Base64
transports binary data efficiently in contexts where only plain text is
allowed.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Use an [ Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html) to decode or encode base64, configured with the base64
alphabet and padding behavior best suited to your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#engine-setup)Engine setup

There is more than one way to encode a stream of bytes as “base64”.
Different applications use different encoding
[alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding behaviors](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-alphabet)Encoding alphabet

Almost all base64 [alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) use `A-Z`, `a-z`, and
`0-9`, which gives nearly 64 characters (26 + 26 + 10 = 62), but they differ
in their choice of their final 2.

Most applications use the [standard](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.STANDARD.html) alphabet specified
in [RFC 4648](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-4).  If that’s all you need, you can get started
quickly by using the pre-configured
[ STANDARD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.STANDARD.html) engine, which is also available
in the

[module as shown here, if you prefer a minimal](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use`
footprint.```
use base64::prelude::*;
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.decode(b"+uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "/+wgVQA=");
```
Other common alphabets are available in the [ alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-safe-alphabet)URL-safe alphabet

The standard alphabet uses `+` and `/` as its two non-alphanumeric tokens,
which cannot be safely used in URL’s without encoding them as `%2B` and
`%2F`.

To avoid that, some applications use a [“URL-safe” alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.URL_SAFE.html),
which uses `-` and `_` instead. To use that alternative alphabet, use the
[ URL_SAFE](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.URL_SAFE.html) engine. This example doesn’t
use

[to show what a more explicit](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use` would look like.```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.decode(b"-uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "_-wgVQA=");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#padding-characters)Padding characters

Each base64 character represents 6 bits (2⁶ = 64) of the original binary data, and every 3 bytes of input binary data will encode to 4 base64 characters (8 bits × 3 = 6 bits × 4 = 24 bits).

When the input is not an even multiple of 3 bytes in length, [canonical](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-3.5)
base64 encoders insert padding characters at the end, so that the output
length is always a multiple of 4:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg==");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8=");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
Canonical encoding ensures that base64 encodings will be exactly the same,
byte-for-byte, regardless of input length. But the `=` padding characters
aren’t necessary for decoding, and they may be omitted by using a
[ NO_PAD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.NO_PAD.html) configuration:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD_NO_PAD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
The pre-configured `NO_PAD` engines will reject inputs containing padding
`=` characters. To encode without padding and still accept padding while
decoding, create an [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with
that [padding mode](https://docs.rs/engine/enum.DecodePaddingMode.html).

`assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.decode(b"Zm8="), Err(base64::DecodeError::InvalidPadding));`[§](https://docs.rs#further-customization)Further customization

Decoding and encoding behavior can be customized by creating an
[engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with an [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding configuration](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html):

```
use base64::{engine, alphabet, Engine as _};
// bizarro-world base64: +/ as the first symbols instead of the last
let alphabet =
    alphabet::Alphabet::new("+/ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789")
    .unwrap();
// a very weird config that encodes with padding but requires no padding when decoding...?
let crazy_config = engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()
    .with_decode_allow_trailing_bits(true)
    .with_encode_padding(true)
    .with_decode_padding_mode(engine::DecodePaddingMode::RequireNone);
let crazy_engine = engine::GeneralPurpose::new(&alphabet, crazy_config);
let encoded = crazy_engine.encode(b"abc 123");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#memory-allocation)Memory allocation

The [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and [encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) engine methods
allocate memory for their results – `decode` returns a `Vec<u8>` and
`encode` returns a `String`. To instead decode or encode into a buffer that
you allocated, use one of the alternative methods:

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding)Decoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::decode` | returns a new `Vec<u8>` | always |
| `Engine::decode_vec` | appends to provided `Vec<u8>` | if `Vec`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::decode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding)Encoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::encode` | returns a new `String` | always |
| `Engine::encode_string` | appends to provided `String` | if `String`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::encode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#input-and-output)Input and output

The `base64` crate can [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and
[encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) values in memory, or
[ DecoderReader](https://docs.rs/read/struct.DecoderReader.html) and

[provide streaming decoding and encoding for any](https://docs.rs/write/struct.EncoderWriter.html)

`EncoderWriter`[readable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)or

[writable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)byte stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding-1)Decoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, read::DecoderReader};
let mut input = io::stdin();
let mut decoder = DecoderReader::new(&mut input, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut decoder, &mut io::stdout())?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-1)Encoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, write::EncoderWriter};
let mut output = io::stdout();
let mut encoder = EncoderWriter::new(&mut output, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut io::stdin(), &mut encoder)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#display)Display

If you only need a base64 representation for implementing the
[ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) trait, use

[:](https://docs.rs/display/struct.Base64Display.html)

`Base64Display````
use base64::{display::Base64Display, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
let value = Base64Display::new(b"\0\x01\x02\x03", &STANDARD);
assert_eq!("base64: AAECAw==", format!("base64: {}", value));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If length calculations result in overflowing `usize`, a panic will result.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use engine::`- [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html)
- Provides [Alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html)and constants for alphabets commonly used in the wild.
- [display](https://docs.rs/display/index.html)
- Enables base64’d output anywhere you might use a `Display`implementation, like a format string.
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- Provides the [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html)abstraction and out of the box implementations.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Preconfigured engines for common use cases.
- [read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Read`to transparently decode base64.
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Write`to transparently handle base64.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur while decoding.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeSliceError.html)- Slice - Error
- Errors that can occur while decoding into a slice.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeSliceError.html)- Slice - Error
- Errors that can occur while encoding into a slice.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode](https://docs.rs/fn.decode.html)- Deprecated
- Decode base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets using the specified [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html).
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Decode the input into the provided output slice.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_vec.html)- engine_ - vec - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets.
- [decoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.decoded_len_estimate.html)- len_ - estimate
- Returns a conservative estimate of the decoded size of `encoded_len`base64 symbols (rounded up to the next group of 3 decoded bytes).
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)- Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the provided `Engine`into a new`String`.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied slice.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_string.html)- engine_ - string - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied `String`.
- [encoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.encoded_len.html)- len
- Calculate the base64 encoded length for a given input length, optionally including any appropriate padding bytes.

# car_proto - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/car-proto/^0.32.0/

## Expand description

JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol types for CAR client-server communication.

The protocol is bidirectional over WebSocket:

- Client → Server: session.init, tools.register, proposal.submit, verify
- Server → Client: tools.execute (callback for tool execution)
- Server → Client: execution.event (notifications)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [daemon](https://docs.rs/daemon/index.html)
- Mechanism helpers for the CAR daemon — URL parsing, probing,
and spawning the `car-server`binary. Hoisted out of`car-cli`and`car-ffi-common::proxy`(#139-fu1) so both sides share one implementation.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Create](https://docs.rs/struct.CreateHostApprovalRequest.html)- Host - Approval - Request
- Request to create an approval prompt in the host surface.
- [Execution](https://docs.rs/struct.ExecutionEvent.html)- Event
- Execution event notification (streaming).
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostAgent.html)- Agent
- Agent entry visible to menu bar, tray, or terminal host clients.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostAgentDisplay.html)- Agent - Display
- Host-visible display hints for an agent.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostApprovalRequest.html)- Approval - Request
- Approval request visible to the OS host surface.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostEvent.html)- Event
- Host event emitted to subscribed OS host clients.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostIdentity.html)- Identity
- Daemon-identifying metadata returned inside `HostSnapshot``car-server install`plus an ad-hoc eval daemon, etc.) tell which daemon they connected to and whether THIS one owns the supervisor lock or is observe-only. Closes the observability gap from Parslee-ai/car-releases#44.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/struct.HostSnapshot.html)- Snapshot
- Snapshot returned by `host.subscribe`.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingConfigSetRequest.html)- Config - SetRequest
- Params for `messaging.config.set`. All fields optional — only the supplied fields mutate (a`null`/absent field leaves that part of the config unchanged).`add_handles`/`remove_handles`apply after`allowlisted_handles`when both are present.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingConfigView.html)- Config - View
- Result of `messaging.config.get`/`messaging.config.set`— the current (or post-mutation) view of the transport config. The active pairing code is intentionally NOT echoed here (it is surfaced only via`messaging.pairing.status`, mirroring the local-UI-rooted invariant).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingPairingStartResponse.html)- Pairing - Start - Response
- Result of `messaging.pairing.start`— the freshly minted, high-entropy pairing code to display ONLY in the local UI, plus the post-mint view.
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingPairingStatusResponse.html)- Pairing - Status - Response
- Result of `messaging.pairing.status`— whether a pairing is in flight and, when so, the active code (host/local-auth gated read only, so the local UI can re-display the code after a reload).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingStatusView.html)- Status - View
- Result of `messaging.status`— the real runtime liveness of a channel’s approval transport, computed daemon-side (U2). The host UI renders a SINGLE readiness state from this object rather than re-deriving “is it on” from scattered permission widgets (the scatter that produced the confusing pane).
- [Messaging](https://docs.rs/struct.MessagingTestSendResponse.html)- Test - Send - Response
- Result of `messaging.test_send`— the synchronous outcome of the on-demand self-test (U4).`ok:true`means the labeled test message was delivered to the paired handle;`ok:false`carries an actionable`error`(channel off, no paired handle, Automation denied, recipient-not-found). The self-test mints NO approval/pairing mapping and resolves nothing.
- [Parslee](https://docs.rs/struct.ParsleeIdentity.html)- Identity
- Parslee cloud identity associated with the local CAR user.
- [Policy](https://docs.rs/struct.PolicyDefinition.html)- Definition
- Policy definition from client.
- [Policy](https://docs.rs/struct.PolicyRejection.html)- Rejection
- A policy rejection captured on a turn (R2 / R11). When an action is
`ActionStatus::Rejected`, the tool body never ran, so`cli_outcome`is forced to`not-run`and the rejection is recorded here.
- [Proposal](https://docs.rs/struct.ProposalSubmitRequest.html)- Submit - Request
- Submit a proposal for execution.
- [Register](https://docs.rs/struct.RegisterHostAgentRequest.html)- Host - Agent - Request
- Request to register an agent with the OS host surface.
- [Resolve](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolveHostApprovalRequest.html)- Host - Approval - Request
- Request to resolve an approval.
- [RunComplete](https://docs.rs/struct.RunCompleteRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.complete`request params.
- [RunComplete](https://docs.rs/struct.RunCompleteResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.complete`response.
- [RunEnded](https://docs.rs/struct.RunEnded.html)
- A run reached a terminal state — recorded on `runs.complete`(with a reported outcome) or on a mid-run disconnect (as`Incomplete`).
- [RunGet](https://docs.rs/struct.RunGetTraceRequest.html)- Trace - Request
- `runs.get_trace`request params — fetch a run’s full ordered trace.
- [RunList](https://docs.rs/struct.RunListRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.list`request params — list an agent’s runs newest-first.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.RunRecordTurnsRequest.html)- Turns - Request
- `runs.record_turns`request params — a WS-only batch append of client-narrated turns to a run the calling connection owns. The agent builds full- `RunTurn`s itself (out-of-pipeline capture: its work happens inside its own subprocess, never through- `proposal.submit`), then pushes them here in batches. The daemon owns the turn- `index`(re-stamped under the- `runs`lock — the client’s- `index`values are ignored), the per-field/per-turn byte caps, the batch-size cap, and the per-run turn ceiling; it appends through the same- `record_run_turns`path the proposal recorder uses, so persistence and- `runs.trace.event`fanout are identical. Turn content beyond size is intentional pass-through — the daemon validates size and ownership, never semantics.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.RunRecordTurnsResponse.html)- Turns - Response
- `runs.record_turns`response.
- [RunStart](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStartRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.start`request params.
- [RunStart](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStartResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.start`response.
- [RunStarted](https://docs.rs/struct.RunStarted.html)
- A run began — recorded when `runs.start`mints the`run_id`.
- [RunSubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunSubscribeRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.subscribe`request params.
- [RunSubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunSubscribeResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.subscribe`response — the snapshot-at-cursor the client folds before the live- `runs.trace.event`stream starts.
- [RunTrace](https://docs.rs/struct.RunTraceEvent.html)- Event
- One `runs.trace.event`server → client notification (agent run tracing, U4). Pushed to every`(host_client, run_id)`subscriber.
- [RunTurn](https://docs.rs/struct.RunTurn.html)
- One captured turn of a run — one action of one submitted proposal.
- [RunUnsubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunUnsubscribeRequest.html)- Request
- `runs.unsubscribe`request params.
- [RunUnsubscribe](https://docs.rs/struct.RunUnsubscribeResponse.html)- Response
- `runs.unsubscribe`response.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionInitRequest.html)- Init - Request
- Initialize a session.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionInitResponse.html)- Init - Response
- [SetHost](https://docs.rs/struct.SetHostAgentStatusRequest.html)- Agent - Status - Request
- Request to update an agent’s host-visible status.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolCancelRequest.html)- Cancel - Request
- Fire-and-forget `tools.cancel`notification (Parslee-ai/car#264).
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolDefinition.html)- Definition
- Tool definition sent by client during registration.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolExecuteRequest.html)- Execute - Request
- Server asks client to execute a tool.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [CliOutcome](https://docs.rs/enum.CliOutcome.html)
- How a CLI-driving action (e.g. Bulldozer’s `drive_cli`) terminated.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostAgentStatus.html)- Agent - Status
- OS-host-visible agent status.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostApprovalStatus.html)- Approval - Status
- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.HostManifestRole.html)- Manifest - Role
- Manifest-lock relationship for the daemon serving this WS.
Returned inside `HostIdentity`
- [RunLive](https://docs.rs/enum.RunLiveStatus.html)- Status
- Coarse live status of a run for the subscribe snapshot and each
`runs.trace.event`. Distinct from the run-level`OutcomeStatus`carried inside a terminal`RunTermination::Outcome`— this is the “is the run still open?” signal the live client folds into its view. Mirrors`RunStore::RunStatus`but lives in`car-proto`so the wire shape doesn’t depend on the server-core crate.
- [RunRecord](https://docs.rs/enum.RunRecord.html)
- One durable run record. U1 ships `Started`/`Ended`; U2 adds the per-turn`Turn`variant. Tagged on`record`so adding a variant is forward-compatible on the wire.
- [RunTermination](https://docs.rs/enum.RunTermination.html)
- How a run reached its terminal state.
- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/enum.VerifierVerdict.html)- Verdict
- The verifier verdict for a turn — Bulldozer’s `check_outcome`result.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [PROTOCOL_](https://docs.rs/constant.PROTOCOL_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- Wire protocol version for the daemon JSON-RPC protocol. Bump ONLY on a
backward-incompatible change to the request/response shapes or method
semantics (NOT on every release — this is independent of the package
semver). Client and server exchange this in the `server.handshake`RPC so version drift FAILS LOUD with a clear error instead of silently misbehaving or hanging.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [deterministic_](https://docs.rs/fn.deterministic_run_id.html)- run_ - id
- Compute a deterministic, content-derived run id (EPIC B / B7).

# futures_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures-util/^0.3/

## Expand description

Combinators and utilities for working with `Future`s, `Stream`s, `Sink`s,
and the `AsyncRead` and `AsyncWrite` traits.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, returning a tuple of all results once complete.
- [pending](https://docs.rs/macro.pending.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which yields to the event loop once.
- [pin_mut](https://docs.rs/macro.pin_mut.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [poll](https://docs.rs/macro.poll.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which returns the result of polling a future once within the
current `async`context.
- [ready](https://docs.rs/macro.ready.html)
- Extracts the successful type of `Poll<T>`.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`and- `std`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. If multiple futures are ready,
one will be pseudo-randomly selected at runtime. Futures directly
passed to `select!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [select_](https://docs.rs/macro.select_biased.html)- biased - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. Unlike `select!``select_biased!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [stream_](https://docs.rs/macro.stream_select.html)- select - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`and- `std`
- Combines several streams, all producing the same `Item`type, into one stream. This is similar to`select_all`but does not require the streams to all be the same type. It also keeps the streams inline, and does not require`Box<dyn Stream>`s to be allocated. Streams passed to this macro must be`Unpin`.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, resolving to a `Result`

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Deserialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
